---
title: Best practices
description: Designing a safe integration, from price selection to latency and stablecoins.
---

[Your responsibilities](/docs/build/responsibilities) lists the checks every contract must make. This
page covers the design decisions behind them.

## Integers and exponents

Prices are integers with an exponent. Rescale to one exponent before comparing or combining, use
128-bit intermediates for products, and round in the direction that favours your protocol.

## Confidence

Every price comes with `conf`. Use it:

- value collateral at `price − conf` and debt at `price + conf`;
- pause or widen spreads when `conf / price` exceeds a threshold;
- expect wider confidence on [thinner-liquidity feeds](/docs/feeds#categories).

## Choosing which update to apply

In a pull oracle, whoever submits the transaction chooses which signed update to use. They cannot
forge one or go backwards, but they can pick any recent one. An attacker might pick the update most
favourable to them from the last few seconds.

- Require prices to be recent: after your cell's creation, or within a small window of a recent
  block (see [Check freshness](/docs/build/guides/freshness)).
- For settlement, require the **exact** tick (`publish_time_ms == T`), which leaves no choice.

## Latency

No on-chain price can be faster than the exchanges. Traders see moves before your contract does.
For derivatives and trading:

- **Delay settlement.** Take an order now, fill it at the first tick after it was placed.
- **Use spreads** based on confidence.
- **Require minimum holding times** before positions can be closed.

## Stablecoins

- A /USDT price is in USDT. If USDT loses its peg, /USDT feeds keep pricing in USDT.
- If you value things in USD, convert with USDT/USD, and consider pausing when USDT/USD moves more
  than a set amount from 1.
- Don't treat BTC/USD, BTC/USDT and BTC/USDC as interchangeable.

## Availability

- Plan for missing ticks and a stalled committee: your contract should fail safe (refuse to act)
  rather than use an old price.
- Configure more than one mirror URL in your application.
- Keep your feed cell's lock and your keeper's key available; nobody else updates your cell.

## Committee changes

Pin the committee type hash, not the set index. After a rotation the type hash stays the same, so
your contract keeps working, and updates from the old keys are refused automatically.
